title: Ajmal v. State of U.P. & 2 Ors.
coram: V.K. Shukla, J. & Mohd. Tahir, J.
docket: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 2714 of 2015
disposition: Writ petition disposed of (FIR not quashed; arrest to follow s.41 CrPC safeguards)
headnote: An FIR under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 that discloses a cognizable offence will not be quashed; but as the offence does not entail imprisonment beyond seven years, any arrest must comply with the safeguards of Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A of the Cr.P.C. The offence being compoundable, the accused may pursue compounding as provided under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The judgment's substantive holding is procedural/criminal; its contribution to Supply Code jurisprudence is limited to noting the Code as the route for compounding.

holding_units.topic: Theft (s.135) compounded through the Supply Code — theft/UUE-Code linkage
holding_units.holding: The offence of electricity theft under Section 135 being compoundable, the accused's compounding remedy lies 'as provided under the provisions of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005' — the Code furnishing the machinery through which theft (Section 135) and, cognately, unauthorised use of electricity (Section 126) are assessed and compounded. Pending compounding, as the offence does not entail imprisonment beyond seven years, any arrest must comply with Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A Cr.P.C.; the FIR, disclosing a cognizable offence, was not quashed.
holding_units.flag: Scope: the case's express Code engagement is the compounding remedy; the operative relief concerned arrest safeguards (s.41(1)(b)/41-A Cr.P.C.). Retained as a node in the theft / unauthorised-use line, which the Supply Code's assessment and compounding machinery governs.

principle_tags.application: A compoundable Section 135 theft offence is to be compounded under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 procedure; the Code supplies the enforcement / compounding machinery for theft (and, cognately, unauthorised use under Section 126).
